If the PS5 picture stays black inside the CouchSubs TV app, choose Overlay: the TV shows the PS5 on its own HDMI input and the subtitles appear on top. If no picture arrives, the TV app first lists its HDMI inputs and switches to Overlay where it can. Overlay also helps if the TV changes its picture mode or drops Game mode or HDR while the TV app is open: inside the app the TV handles the PS5 picture as an app, not as its HDMI input. The TV app from Google Play has no Overlay mode: there this choice is not applied and the TV says so on screen.

Translation to the TV keeps going when the phone is locked or the screen turns off. While the screen is off, though, Wi-Fi switches to power saving, and on some phones the connection can slow down or drop. The most reliable way is to leave the screen on and turn the brightness down.
Translation may stop when the phone locks

Battery restrictions are on for CouchSubs on this phone. When the screen turns off, the phone\'s battery saver can slow down or cut the connection, or stop translation. In the settings that open, set CouchSubs to Unrestricted under Battery. On Vivo, Xiaomi and Oppo, also allow it to run in the background and to auto-start.
Keep the PS5, TV and phone on the same network
With your own account, on the TV

When Remote Play connects with the same account, it takes over your session and controller. The second account only receives the picture; you keep playing with your own account and controller. The account is free, no PS Plus needed.
Turn on the game\'s own subtitles: CouchSubs reads the English subtitles on screen, not the audio.

When you turn on the controller to play, choose your MAIN account on the PS5. Don\'t play with the second account CouchSubs signs in with, or the controller will turn off by itself or won\'t work in the game.

If no pack recognises the game, asked once two minutes after translation starts.
Keeps the character\'s name in front of the translation (ARTHUR: …). The name itself is never translated.
Check unchanged subtitle areas more often
When the subtitle area looks unchanged, read it again after 2 frames instead of 20. Uses more CPU.
Play Xbox sound on this device

While remote play is running, the Xbox mutes the TV and sends game sound only to this device (an Xbox limitation). If you turn this off, the game has no sound. To hear it from the TV or speakers, connect this phone to a Bluetooth speaker or headphones.
Screen stays on · brightness dims automatically
The pack is chosen automatically when the game opens. Lines not in the pack are translated with your chosen engine. Packs are free; new ones and fixes download automatically.
New packs and fixes download automatically once a week
Example: Translate swear words without softening them.
Added to the end of the AI translator\'s instructions (up to 1000 characters). Leave it empty if you don\'t need it.
In games with a ready pack, this engine only translates missing lines.
Drag the slider all the way to the end to make the background fully solid and hide the English subtitle in the game. A full-width band also covers the sides.
Cover: the translation hides the English subtitle in the game. Choose Above or Below to see the English subtitle too, with the translation right above or below it.
A sample subtitle appears on the TV when you let go of the slider. In fixed position you can also move subtitles with the ▲ and ▼ buttons on the TV remote.
Only needed if the second account has a login passcode on the PS5. CouchSubs enters it when the PS5 asks; it is stored encrypted on the phone.

3. Turn Developer mode On, type this phone\'s address as Host PC IP and press OK:

4. Restart the TV: hold the power button on the remote and keep holding until the TV turns off and comes back on with the Samsung logo (about 5 seconds); letting go when it turns off only puts it on standby. If no logo appears, unplug the TV for 30 seconds.

CouchSubs opens its waiting screen on the TV. Even if it mentions a computer, that is not an error: the TV is waiting for the phone. Now tap Start translation on the home screen; the TV finds this phone by itself.
CouchSubs %1$s is already on the TV; opening it.
If the page doesn\'t appear, tap Open in browser above to sign in in your phone\'s browser.

If the TV shows “Server under maintenance”, it cannot reach Samsung\'s servers: check the TV\'s internet connection and its date and time, restart the TV and try again.

The TV did not accept this phone. In the TV\'s Developer mode window, check that Host PC IP is this phone\'s address (%1$s), then restart the TV fully: hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears (about 5 seconds), or unplug the TV for 30 seconds.

The TV (%1$s) and this phone (%2$s) are on different networks, so the TV refuses the phone. Connect both to the same Wi-Fi (not a guest network or a second router), type the phone\'s new address as Host PC IP on the TV, then restart the TV fully (hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears, about 5 seconds).

The TV\'s settings are right (Developer mode on, Host PC IP %1$s), but the TV has not fully restarted since then, so it does not accept the phone yet. Hold the power button on the remote until the TV turns off and comes back on with the Samsung logo (about 5 seconds), or unplug the TV for 30 seconds, then try again.

The TV\'s Host PC IP is %1$s, but this phone\'s address is %2$s. In the TV\'s Developer mode window, set Host PC IP to %2$s, then restart the TV fully (hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears, about 5 seconds).

Developer mode is off on the TV. Turn it on with the steps above, type this phone\'s address (%1$s) as Host PC IP, then restart the TV fully (hold the power button until the Samsung logo appears, about 5 seconds).
This Samsung TV is too old for the CouchSubs TV app (2016 models and later are supported).

The TV did not accept the signing certificate. Make sure the TV is connected to the internet (it checks the certificate with Samsung) and its date and time are right (Settings › General › System Manager › Time), then try again. CouchSubs gets a new certificate, so you sign in to Samsung once more.
The TV\'s clock is behind, so the new certificate is not valid for it yet. Set the TV\'s date and time (Settings › General › System Manager › Time) or wait a few minutes, then try again.

The TV refuses CouchSubs because an earlier CouchSubs is still registered on it (Tizen error 118, -22), even if it no longer appears among the apps. If CouchSubs is among the TV\'s apps, delete it there and try again. Otherwise reset Smart Hub (Settings › Support › Device Care › Self Diagnosis › Reset Smart Hub) and try again. Resetting Smart Hub also removes the other apps you downloaded.
The connection to the TV dropped during the install. Keep the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi as this phone, keep the phone\'s screen on, then try again.

Needs LG\'s Developer Mode app on the TV and a free LG developer account. CouchSubs extends the developer mode session for you.
No LG TV found. Is the TV on and on the same Wi-Fi? You can also type its address below (on the TV: Settings › General › Network › the connected network).
Passphrase (key saved; type it if needed)
Turn on developer mode on the TV
1. Create a free LG developer account at webostv.developer.lge.com.
2. On the TV, install the Developer Mode app from the LG Content Store, open it, sign in with your account and turn on Dev Mode Status. The TV restarts.
3. Open the Developer Mode app again and turn on Key Server. Leave the app on screen; a 6-character Passphrase appears at the bottom left.
4. Type the Passphrase above and press Install and open. The passphrase is only needed for the first install.

Developer mode stays on for at most 1000 hours. The phone does not extend it: before it runs out, press EXTEND in the TV\'s Developer Mode app (CouchSubs on a computer does this by itself). If it runs out, the TV app is removed.
The TV did not respond. Make sure the TV is on and on the same Wi-Fi as this phone, and that Dev Mode Status is on in the Developer Mode app.

Next to the pairing code, type the IP address and port from the pairing window too (e.g. 192.168.1.20:37099).
Turn on debugging on the TV
1. Turn on developer options: on the TV, open Settings › System (or Device Preferences) › About and press the Android TV OS build row 7 times.
2. In Settings › System › Developer options, turn on USB debugging. Some TVs also have “Network debugging” or “ADB over network”; turn that on too.

3. Press Install and open. When the TV asks “Allow USB debugging?”, tick “Always allow from this device” and choose Allow. If it cannot connect, try the Wireless debugging option (Android 11 and later, Google TV).
2. Turn on Developer options › Wireless debugging and open it. Type the “IP address & Port” at the top as the TV\'s address.
3. The first time, press “Pair device with pairing code”; type the IP address and port from that window together with the 6-digit code, and press Install and open while the window is still open.

Pairing failed: the code is wrong or the pairing window on the TV closed. Open the window again, type the new code and port and try again.

The button below removes the TV\'s copy and installs the new one; the TV app\'s settings are deleted. If that fails, on the TV go to Settings › Apps › CouchSubs TV › Uninstall, then press Install and open here.

The old CouchSubs TV could not be removed from the TV, so the new one cannot be installed. Remove it on the TV yourself: Settings › Apps › See all apps › CouchSubs TV › Uninstall. Then press Install and open here.

Besides the subtitle, CouchSubs can keep reading up to three small areas, like a quest, a phone message or a notification. Each area is read about once a second and translated again only when its text changes. The translation shows on the TV and on this phone\'s subtitle screen, where the original text is.
